observation.visible_scene: A close-up, backlit view of an agricultural sprinkler operating in a field, framed by large dark green leaves in the foreground (a broad leaf with a curled tip at center-left and another leaf edge at right). The sprinkler head sits on a vertical post on the right side, against a backdrop of trees and a bright, hazy sky. A fan of water spray is thrown from the head toward the upper-left and outward, with individual droplets and a glowing mist illuminated by the backlight. The camera and the foreground leaves remain fixed throughout; the background trees do not shift, indicating no camera motion.
visible_changes: The sprinkler is already spraying at the first frame and continues spraying to the last; no start or stop is shown.

The direction of the main water jet sweeps back and forth over time: it alternates between pointing left/upper-left as a defined stream (e.g., frames 1, 3-9, 13-17, 21-26, 29-34, 37-41) and pointing more toward the viewer as a diffuse, forward burst (e.g., frames 2, 10-12, 18-20, 27-28, 35-36), consistent with an oscillating or rotating sprinkler head.

The spray plume continuously expands outward from the nozzle and breaks into scattered droplets and mist; the overall arc of droplets to the right of the head persists while the bright jet changes angle.
Backlighting on the water mist varies in brightness as the spray pattern shifts, but the scene's lighting and leaf silhouettes stay essentially constant.
Foreground leaves and background trees show no positional change, confirming the apparent motion belongs to the water and the sprinkler head, not to the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the spray (water pressure source, pump) is not visible.
Whether the head's motion is a full rotation or a limited oscillation cannot be determined from this segment.
What happens before t=0 and after t=1.6 s (onset, shutdown, or continued cycling) is unknown.
The identity of the crop/field and any operator are unseen.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation angle and speed of the sprinkler head.
Any very slight sway of the leaves (motion, if present, is negligible and not clearly distinguishable from static).
Whether some bright streaks are reflections on wet leaf edges or airborne droplets.
